01 / EXPERIMENT DESIGN

A model you can inspect

This app runs the same training-only pipelines as the Python portfolio project. The target is a simulated transition to 90+ days past due within 90 days. It is not legal default, and the probabilities have not been calibrated or validated against real borrower outcomes.

TRAINJan–Mar 2025

1,430 accounts
Outcomes mature by June 29

VALIDATEJuly 2025

508 accounts
Outcomes mature by October 29

TESTNov–Dec 2025

995 accounts
Outcomes mature by March 31, 2026

Another 3,067 snapshots are excluded to preserve these gaps. Account and customer IDs are disjoint across splits. Median imputation, standardization, and category encoding are fitted on the training split only.

Logistic regression was selected using validation ROC-AUC. Its 26% threshold maximized validation F2 on a fixed 0.10–0.80 grid, an illustrative objective that emphasizes recall. The same threshold is offered for the random forest as a scenario, not a separately optimized operating point.

02 / EXPLANATIONS & LIMITS

Understand what the visuals mean

Logistic explanations show signed feature contributions to log-odds, relative to standardized training means, plus portfolio encoding. They sum with the intercept to the model’s score; they are not percentage-point effects or causal explanations.

Random forest explanations show the selected logistic model’s global permutation importance, clearly labeled as such. Permutation importance is the mean decrease in test ROC-AUC over eight shuffles; correlated features can affect interpretation. No individual random forest attribution is claimed.

Input bounds allow exploratory scenarios. The app marks values outside observed training ranges, where estimates are less supported. Missing income uses the training median. Enter only synthetic examples; this is a portfolio demonstration, not a lending decision system.
